entries.why: B presents a complete metropolitan region with layered shorelines, bridges, forests, districts and atmospheric depth. A has readable roads and a core, but large empty grass parcels, repeated towers and thin vegetation make it look like a compact simulation fixture.
entries.loserNeeds: Increase real block-frontage density and asset variation while retaining the readable district plan.

entries.why: A has believable house lots, varied trees and hedges, strong contact shadows, road camber and fine material detail. B communicates a suburb but the water tower, white civic blocks, repeated small houses and card-like trees expose coarse geometry and weak grounding.
entries.loserNeeds: Replace the repeated house/foliage set with grounded, materially varied lots and articulated civic assets.

entries.why: A has precise road geometry, lane markings, barriers, vehicles, deep tree shadows and convincing construction feedback. B shows a coherent interchange but its shoulders, merging geometry, vegetation and surrounding lots lack the detail and material response needed at this scale.
entries.loserNeeds: Raise road-edge, junction and vegetation fidelity so the interchange holds up as the main subject.

entries.why: B builds a convincing night street from wet reflections, signs, lamps, traffic and pedestrians at several depths. A has readable lit windows and streets, but white window panels, weak pools of light and almost no visible activity leave it feeling like an unoccupied architectural model.
entries.loserNeeds: Add grounded warm light sources, reflected/wet material response and concentrated street-level activity.
